answer: Each identity posts an 80 bond for one river voyage carrying jade and files barge draft readings. An auditor recomputes weight from the displacement table and checks the river gauge; a mismatch above 2% burns the bond. The first fake pays 80 plus 29; the k-th pays 29+9(k-1), since each voyage needs a new hull, draft pair, and timestamp. The 1000th fake costs 9020, and 1000 fakes cost 4,524,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked bonds. A rented-barge ring fails: reusing one hull and draft pair collides on hull number and timestamp, so duplicates are slashed. An honest carrier pays one bond plus 29.
